items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, adversarially both ways. The opening verse is three tokens in full, "וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף" (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier, collate-verified): a waw-conjunctive definite noun phrase carrying no hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative, or temporal-formula onset; the staged parashah inventory carries no seg at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18 (nearest segs: SAMEKH at Isa.2.11, PE at Isa.2.22, single witness, tier-3), so the 2:17|2:18 seam has neither a tier-1 onset nor a tier-3 mark, absence weighed only as absence of support. The shipped oss entries (oracle_frame.concluding_summary, parashah.pe_boundary) both attach to the 2:22 close, and the boundary_rationale's sole opening warrant is the quoted 'fresh topical turn'. Continuity across the seam also re-derives: "בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙" opens oshb:Isa.2.20 verse-initial (byte tier) — the span's only verse-initial temporal formula, two verses past the seam — and the flight core "מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר" collates byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 3 verses, accent_stripped tier), straddling the seam; frontier_flag_considered is false. High is the filed and correct severity: the row's own load-bearing opening boundary rests on topical shift alone. Span ruling — endorse the routing proposal for the owner docket, adopting nothing: branch (a) is byte-sound as a one-edit seam-pair cure — a merged Isa.2.12-Isa.2.22 opens on the verse-initial temporal-formula onset "כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת" (oshb:Isa.2.12, byte tier) and closes at the PE seg at Isa.2.22 (single witness, tier-3 corroboration) with the fresh onset "כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת" standing at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier) — at the recorded cost, already disclosed as a live rival in the neighbour row's own device_notes, of reading the 2:17 refrain as internal punctuation rather than a unit close; branch (b) is byte-unsound and should be recorded so: it would sever the eight-token run "מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ", byte-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), across its new 2:19|2:20 seam and leave a 2:12-2:19 remainder closing on no signal; branch (c) is the disclosure-only fallback if the owner declines any respan. Any replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original.

Both legs re-derive. The mark is real and honestly labelled where cited (the staged parashah inventory records PE at Isa.2.22; the boundary_rationale discloses it single-witness, tier-3), but the row promotes it to a bounder: the strongest_rejected_alternative makes 'the petuchah break closing the chapter' one of the two grounds that bound the unit, and the oss key is parashah.pe_boundary, where sibling rows in this corpus carry corroboration-style parashah keys — under the owner addendum the Prophets parashah layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never bounds. Meanwhile the genuine tier-1 rear-seam signal, "כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת" (oshb:Isa.3.1, tokens 1-5, verse-initial, byte tier, collate-verified), is neither quoted nor carried: the row's boundary_evidence_refs contain no Isa.3.1 entry under either witness prefix. Medium is right: the 2:22|3:1 seam itself is sound — the next row opens on that hinneh onset — so this is a mis-tiered warrant plus a missing tier-1 citation, defective but not alone load-bearing.

Re-swept from the pointed splice "ה֣וֹי" (oshb:Isa.5.20, token 1, byte tier at its own site): 5 verses byte / 21 accent_stripped / 22 skeleton (sweep: verse counts) — the filed digits re-derive exactly. The skeleton 22 is a token-verse object, not an onset object: verse-initial stands at 20, matching the staged device inventory's own 22-token-verse against 20-verse-initial split, and one of the 22 is Isa.16.4, whose matching token sits mid-verse in "מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי סֵ֥תֶר" (oshb:Isa.16.4, tokens 4-6, byte tier) — the splice "ה֣וֹי" collates against oshb:Isa.16.4 only at skeleton tier, i.e. the 16:4 token is the differently-pointed be-verb imperative, not the hoy interjection, exactly as the inventory's role-split note flags ('16:4? no — verify per site'). That role split leaves the woe-oracle onset subclass at 18 (the ch-5 six, the 28-33 six, plus 10:1, 10:5, 17:12, 18:1, 45:9, 45:10). So 'the hoy-onset lexeme stands at 22 verses' names an object matching neither the counted skeleton token-verse object (not onset-bound, not lexeme-pure) nor the onset subclass. The same sentence's oy discipline re-verifies exactly: standalone-token object 4 verses (Isa.3.9, Isa.3.11, Isa.6.5, Isa.24.16) against a bare three-consonant substring object of 8, the extra four being contained-consonant hits at Isa.1.24, Isa.26.9, Isa.35.8, Isa.63.10 (sweep: verse counts, skeleton tier). Medium is right: a role-blended count object in device_notes; no boundary rests on the digit, and the proposed restatement applies the sentence's own oy discipline to hoy.

The warrant is load-bearing by the row's own construction: the boundary_rationale demotes the only formal signal at the seam ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own') and rests the rear seam on the frame-mode characterisation instead. Re-derived at the characterised cycle's close: oshb:Isa.7.25 carries "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (byte tier, collate-verified), which the campaign's second witness renders as direct second-person address, “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — inside the very range the row characterises as addressing no one directly and itself cites (web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25). The facing row for that range carries the identical warrant sentence two sentences from its own 'addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative', with a rejected-alternative ground that 'the four share one addressee'. The finding's honest limit re-verifies too: the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the 2ms/3fs parse of the form cannot be machine-settled from the pointed bytes — an unverifiable characterisation cannot carry a load-bearing seam, and the witness-rendering contradiction stands under either parse. High confirmed: a load-bearing rear-seam warrant byte-false under the row's own second witness. The seam placement is not the defect — "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" opens oshb:Isa.7.18 verse-initial (byte tier) and the staged parashah inventory records PE at Isa.7.17 (single witness, tier-3), matching the proposed re-argument.

Re-derived: oshb:Isa.7.12 opens verse-initial on "וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז" (byte tier, collate-verified) — a fifth verse-initial speech onset inside the span, unnamed by the row — and oshb:Isa.7.2 opens on the report formula "וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר" (byte tier). A first-token scan of oshb:Isa.7.1-Isa.7.17 confirms the unqualified class 'verse-initial speech onsets' counts five vayomer/koh-amar/resumptive-speech onsets (7:3, 7:7, 7:10, 7:12, 7:13) even before the 7:2 report formula is weighed, while the four the row names (oshb:Isa.7.3, 7.7, 7.10, 7.13) are the divine/prophetic frame onsets — the object that needed naming under the campaign's semantic-class count discipline, which requires the swept object named before the digit. Medium is right: the digit is not load-bearing — the royal reply at 7:12 sits inside the same third-person narrative frame and reopens nothing — so this is a defective digit-object claim, cured by naming the object or restating the digit, exactly as proposed.

The row's own splices defeat the blanket ground. "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.7.13 (byte tier, collate-verified): speech formula plus imperative plus vocative — a shim'u call, a ruled tier-1 onset class in this book's frame spine — and the addressee shifts across it from the 2ms suffix of "שְׁאַל לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת" (oshb:Isa.7.11, byte tier; “Ask a sign of Yahweh your God;” (web:Isa.7.11), the king addressed singular) to the 2mp suffix of "הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier; “Is it not enough for you” (web:Isa.7.13), the house of David addressed plural) — suffix-form readings argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, no morphology layer being staged. So 'no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene' is contradicted by the row's own cited evidence for the speech complex that carries the sign; the ground survives only if restricted to the rival's exact cut, where oshb:Isa.7.14 opens on "לָ֠כֵן" (byte tier), a continuation particle rather than a fresh frame — which is what the proposed restriction records. Medium is right: the span itself holds under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule; only the stated ground fails.

All the contradictions re-derive inside this one row's fields. The load-bearing front-seam warrant ('best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence ... but from a frame-mode shift', characterising the cycle as one that 'names no speaker and addresses no one directly') is followed two sentences later by 'one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative'; the rejected alternative adds 'the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift'; and the row's own closing quotation renders the direct address the warrant denies — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — against "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" at oshb:Isa.7.25 (byte tier, collate-verified). With no morphology layer staged, the 2ms/3fs parse of the form cannot be machine-settled from the pointed bytes, which itself disqualifies the characterisation as a seam-carrier; the in-field self-contradiction stands under either parse. High confirmed: the row's nominated front-seam warrant is byte-false under its own quoted witness and self-contradicted in-field. The seam placement is not the defect — "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" opens oshb:Isa.7.18 verse-initial (byte tier), and its accent_stripped identity with the openers of oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 collate-verifies at that tier — so the cure is the proposed re-argument plus the confidence reconsideration, not a respan.

Re-swept from splices of oshb:Isa.7.18. The extended opener "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (byte tier at its own verse) sweeps 13 verses at accent_stripped tier (sweep: verse counts) — the row's first digit re-verifies exactly. The bare form "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (byte tier at its own verse) sweeps 12 verses byte / 41 accent_stripped / 45 skeleton (sweep: verse counts); the four verses separating 45 from 41 are exactly MT 2:11, 2:17, 3:7, 29:18, where the form's meteg-bearing pointing survives accent stripping — the staged accent_stripped tier retains meteg, stripping cantillation only — and blocks the accent-tier match, precisely as the finding states. So the shipped 45-verse bare-form digit is the consonantal-skeleton count standing with no tier label of its own inside a parenthetical whose only named tier is accent-stripped, under which the true digit is 41 — a violation of the tier-label law that binds every recurrence claim. Medium is right: the row expressly declines to argue the seam from this recurrence in the same field, so the digit is not load-bearing; either proposed restatement cures it.
